reference: A real Minimoog Model D set to this chart and played by SynthMania ("Minimoog Sound Charts by Tom Rhea", YouTube, copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). My rebuild plays the same notes, transcribed from the recording.
source: Tom Rhea's Sound Charts for the Minimoog (Moog Music, 1974), page 15: oscillators, levels and switches as charted; the cutoff from the dial by the service manual's calibration. source: Tom Rhea's Sound Charts for the Minimoog (Moog Music, 1974), page 15: ranges, levels and switches as charted. Fitted to the recording: the pulse width (that instrument's square wave is nearer a third than a half), cutoff, emphasis, the contour's reach and time, and the glide time.

title: Prophet-5: Sync II
reference: A real Prophet-5 Rev 3 playing factory program 32, recorded by SynthMania (copyrighted: kept in the audition folder for this comparison only). Four single notes cut out of the demonstration, three low and one high (the player bends most of the high ones with the pitch wheel, so they cannot be compared); my rebuild plays the same notes for the same lengths, each at the pitch the recording has it (that instrument is a fifth of a semitone sharp, and further off in its top octaves).
source: Sequential's own factory data for program 3-2 (the 2020 Prophet-5's factory bank, which holds the original forty programs, and the 1978 patch sheet), with the service manual's calibration: oscillators, pulse width, Poly-Mod depth, envelope shape. The filter envelope's reach, the cutoff and the decay time are fitted to the recording.

title: Prophet-5: Brass
reference: No reference beside it, at your choice: every recording of a real Prophet-5 playing this program that I found is short stabs and chords. Five single notes, then three chords.
source: Sequential's own factory data for program 1-1 with the service manual's calibration. The filter envelope's reach is the documents' 5.6 octaves; cutoff and decay time follow what the same model's Sync II needed to match its recording.
